problem_text:
A manufacturing consortium seeks to design a quality improvement plan to reduce total defective output from several production lines. Initially, no corrective measures have been implemented.

The characteristics of each production line are as follows:
* For Line 1, defect rate is 0.747, throughput is 282.553.
* For Line 2, defect rate is 1.928, throughput is 102.185.
* For Line 3, defect rate is 2.591, throughput is 172.851.
* For Line 4, defect rate is 2.145, throughput is 272.442.
* For Line 5, defect rate is 1.815, throughput is 69.989.
* For Line 6, defect rate is 2.253, throughput is 250.255.
* For Line 7, defect rate is 1.14, throughput is 65.175.
* For Line 8, defect rate is 1.416, throughput is 189.505.
* For Line 9, defect rate is 2.015, throughput is 284.561.
* For Line 10, defect rate is 0.677, throughput is 153.988.

To mitigate defects, several quality enhancement protocols are available, each characterized by a specific defect reduction effectiveness:
* By using Protocol1, defects will be reduced by 60%
* By using Protocol2, defects will be reduced by 33%
* By using Protocol3, defects will be reduced by 24%
* By using Protocol4, defects will be reduced by 69%
* By using Protocol5, defects will be reduced by 87%
* By using Protocol6, defects will be reduced by 84%
* By using Protocol7, defects will be reduced by 66%
* By using Protocol8, defects will be reduced by 14%
* By using Protocol9, defects will be reduced by 13%
* By using Protocol10, defects will be reduced by 82%

Implementing a protocol on a line incurs an additional cost per unit of throughput. The cost structure for all line–protocol combinations is summarized below:

| Line \ Protocol | Protocol1 | Protocol2 | Protocol3 | Protocol4 | Protocol5 | Protocol6 | Protocol7 | Protocol8 | Protocol9 | Protocol10 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Line 1 | 147.783 | 111.016 | 45.997 | 109.976 | 57.265 | 128.812 | 43.991 | 152.347 | 88.885 | 30.048 |
| Line 2 | 131.339 | 78.013 | 97.157 | 136.396 | 177.737 | 41.694 | 44.275 | 86.296 | 74.127 | 40.054 |
| Line 3 | 199.702 | 94.172 | 76.942 | 69.879 | 198.378 | 71.684 | 80.627 | 155.195 | 91.812 | 147.915 |
| Line 4 | 125.599 | 116.997 | 50.646 | 155.485 | 185.968 | 58.277 | 192.714 | 95.025 | 85.447 | 148.0 |
| Line 5 | 196.762 | 123.195 | 108.346 | 198.748 | 67.35 | 67.063 | 52.158 | 172.587 | 14.123 | 166.169 |
| Line 6 | 141.047 | 62.432 | 115.196 | 115.701 | 185.925 | 39.396 | 17.17 | 77.575 | 36.298 | 79.746 |
| Line 7 | 120.61 | 54.269 | 164.104 | 27.462 | 85.962 | 184.398 | 149.511 | 147.48 | 160.652 | 42.851 |
| Line 8 | 166.884 | 141.023 | 119.484 | 182.455 | 123.094 | 67.075 | 148.85 | 119.494 | 24.911 | 20.625 |
| Line 9 | 156.471 | 76.107 | 165.257 | 89.139 | 174.888 | 175.259 | 53.076 | 134.028 | 124.437 | 12.173 |
| Line 10 | 157.71 | 82.673 | 67.909 | 17.825 | 112.587 | 38.42 | 105.456 | 51.951 | 19.599 | 149.0 |

Please determine how to apply the quality protocols to each production line (lines may adopt multiple protocols simultaneously), and note that a line may also remain partially uncorrected if necessary. The objective is to ensure that the total defective output is reduced by at least a proportion P = 0.396 of the initial defect level, while minimizing the total implementation cost.
